  <P>
  <span class="subtitle">Hackers :: Toolchain</span>
  </p><span class="bodytext">

<p>
You can get a precompiled toolchain (BSP) from TimeSys, after (free) registration: <p>
<a href="http://www.timesys.com/index.cfm?hdr=linux_header.cfm&bdy=linux_bdy_download.cfm&item_id=78">http://www.timesys.com/index.cfm?hdr=linux_header.cfm&bdy=linux_bdy_download.cfm&item_id=78</a>
<br>Trust me, registering is much faster and easier than building your own ;-)<p>
<span class="subtitle">Build your own</span>
<p>If you want to build your own, I strongly suggest to take a look at <a href="/~jal0/">jal0's pages</a> for detailed instructions.

</p>
<p>
Below are the outdated instructions to build you own on Linux, based on instructions from Bradley D. LaRonde (<a href="http://www.ltc.com/~brad/mips/mipsel-linux-cross-toolchain-building.txt">http://www.ltc.com/~brad/mips/mipsel-linux-cross-toolchain-building.txt</a>) 
</p>
<p>
If you want to use a Win32 host instead of a linux host, please take a look at 
<a href="/~jal0/">jal0's instructions</a>
</p>
<p>
<span class="code">
<br># get the files
<br>wget ftp://ftp.kernel.org/pub/linux/devel/binutils/binutils-2.11.92.0.12.3.tar.gz
<br>wget ftp://ftp.gnu.org/gnu/gcc/gcc-3.0.3/gcc-3.0.3.tar.gz
<br>wget ftp://ftp.gnu.org/gnu/glibc/glibc-2.2.4.tar.gz
<br>wget ftp://ftp.gnu.org/gnu/glibc/glibc-linuxthreads-2.2.4.tar.gz
<br>wget http://www.linux4.BE/download/toolchain/kernel-headers-mipsel-linux-2.4.0-test9-1lv.i386.rpm
<br>
<br># Build the cross-binutils
<br>tar -xzf binutils-2.11.92.0.12.3.tar.gz
<br>mkdir mipsel-binutils
<br>cd mipsel-binutils
<br>../binutils-2.11.92.0.12.3/configure --target=mipsel-linux \
<br>  --libdir='${exec_prefix}'/mipsel-linux/i386-linux/lib
<br>make
<br>make install
<br>cd ..
<br>
<br># Build the C cross-compiler
<br>tar -xzf gcc-3.0.3.tar.gz
<br>mkdir mipsel-gcc
<br>cd mipsel-gcc
<br>#../gcc-3.0.3/configure --target=mipsel-linux --enable-languages=c \
<br>#  --disable-shared --with-headers=/usr/local/mipsel-linux/include
<br>../gcc-3.0.3/configure --target=mipsel-linux --enable-languages=c \
<br>  --disable-shared --with-headers=/home/filip/vr/snow-gcc/mipsel-linux/include/
<br>make
<br>make install
<br>cd ..
<br>
<br># Cross-build glibc
<br>tar -xzf glibc-2.2.4.tar.gz
<br>cd glibc-2.2.4
<br>tar -xzf ../glibc-linuxthreads-2.2.4.tar.gz
<br>cd ..
<br>mkdir mipsel-glibc
<br>cd mipsel-glibc
<br>../glibc-2.2.4/configure --build=i686-linux --host=mipsel-linux \
<br>  --enable-add-ons --prefix=/usr --disable-sanity-checks
<br>make
<br>make install install_root=/usr/local/mipsel-linux/glibc
<br>cd ..
<br>cp -a /usr/local/mipsel-linux/glibc/lib/* /usr/local/mipsel-linux/lib/
<br>cp -a /usr/local/mipsel-linux/glibc/usr/include/* /usr/local/mipsel-linux/include/
<br>cp -a /usr/local/mipsel-linux/glibc/usr/lib/* /usr/local/mipsel-linux/lib/
<br>
<br># Copying the files isn't quite enough though. You also need to edit /usr/local/
<br># mipsel-linux/lib/libc.so (yes, it is a text file suprisingly enough) to point
<br># to the cross-built glibc files so that the cross-build tools know to use the
<br># mipsel libc and not the host's libc, something like:
<br>#
<br># GROUP ( /usr/local/mipsel-linux/lib/libc.so.6
<br>#  /usr/local/mipsel-linux/lib/libc_nonshared.a )
<br>
<br># Build the final C and C++ cross-compilers
<br>cd mipsel-gcc
<br>../gcc-3.0.3/configure --target=mipsel-linux --enable-languages=c,c++
<br>make
<br>make install
<br>
</span>
<br>and that's all ...
<br>
